correctness.rationale: For every nontrivial S(2,k,v), an explicit colour-compatible equitable partition is constructed for 0<=t<=k marked points on one block: the point cells are t named singletons, the remaining k-t block points, and the v-k off-block points; the block cells are the distinguished block, t classes of size r-1, an optional class of size (k-t)(r-1), and a disjoint class of size b-1-k(r-1), with r=(v-1)/(k-1), b=vr/k. All intra/inter-cell incidences are derived from pair uniqueness and therefore are parameter-only. Matching equitable templates force identical complete C2 sentence theories. For STS noncollinear anchors, pair-block and completion-point selectors use 2 variables and ranks 1 and 2, giving a rank-4 Pasch sentence. For the explicit PG(3,2) versus Z5xZ3 Bose designs, all pair incidences and all 455 triples were exhaustively checked; an independent enumeration of all 52360 four-block subsets gives 105 versus 0 Pasches. Round-0,1,2 joint refinement histograms agree, and first differ at round 3, establishing exact sentence rank 4. Both standalone programs executed successfully, with no extrapolation from finite checks to universal claims.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the all-parameter blockwise landmark-blindness theorem for Steiner-design incidence graphs, together with a sharp 3-mark and quantifier-rank-4 Pasch contrast for explicit order-15 systems. The general 2015 C2/equitable-partition and amenability results establish tools but their inspected portions and full-text searches do not give the design-specific equitable incidence table or this sharp boundary. The anti-Pasch 2000 publication discusses combinatorial constructions, not the counting-logic landmark threshold in accessible material. Published scientific-record searches for the objects, aliases, marked-point parameters, rank, and implications found Pasch census and Steiner-incidence topology results but no covering logical theorem. This remains best-knowledge originality, not a certified priority or independence claim.

value.rationale: The Pasch quadruple is the canonical smallest nontrivial configuration in a Steiner triple system. The result identifies a natural information boundary for vertex-landmark individualization: marking any part, even all points, of a single block leaves all Steiner 2-designs with fixed parameters indistinguishable in C2, while three noncollinear points expose Pasch structure with a uniform rank-four formula. The explicit order-15 projective/Bose contrast shows the landmark number three and logical depth four are attained sharply. This is an all-size structural phenomenon coupled to a motivated, smallest obstruction, not a table recomputation or cosmetic parameter change.
